header:
Date: 2026-08-04 15:00 EDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Claire Huang (Beta Lane, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Beta Lane, Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Beta Lane, Security), Ethan Brooks (Beta Lane, PM)
Recording: yes
Links shared: https://redwood.app/links/pilot-benchmarks , https://drive.company/beta-lane/pilot-runbook-v1
transcript:
[00:00:01] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call?
[00:00:07] Claire Huang: Claire here.
[00:00:09] Marcus Lee: Marcus.
[00:00:11] Priya Desai: Priya, SE from Redwood.
[00:00:13] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia from security.
[00:00:15] Ethan Brooks: Ethan, PM.
[00:00:18] Alex Morgan: Great. Agenda: quick recap of last week's fixes, 72-hour benchmark review, tail-latency root causes, then canary/cutover plan and runbook changes. Priya, you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:00:32] Priya Desai: Yeah sure. So we ran the three 24-hour windows mimicking your prod traffic shape, thank you Marcus for the traces. Median latency sat around 62ms for the redwood-ggml-q4fp model variant, p95 at 130ms, p99 at 410ms on the largest bursts. We saw the tail coincide with small spikes in sequence length and sudden concurrent requests on warmup windows, plus one instance of a GC-ish pause on the host.
[00:01:02] Marcus Lee: Right, that matches what we saw on the platform side--we have short bursts from the webhooks where 20-30 extra requests hit in 10s.
[00:01:12] Claire Huang: Is that the KV cache cold start causing the jump? We thought your prefix caching would cover that.
[00:01:18] Priya Desai: Partly. The prefix KV cache helps but only once requests share prefixes. In a high-cardinality session the initial kv lookups and the kernel compilation path for longer sequences caused extra latency. Also, our batching threshold was set conservatively to meet median latency, which increased p99 under burst.
[00:01:38] Alex Morgan: So mitigation steps we tried this week were: reduce batch timeout to 12ms, enable proactive KV prefetch for known session tokens, and apply a quantization profile that trades a small accuracy delta for lower memory bandwidth. The first two reduced p99 in two of the windows to ~260ms but one window still spiked to ~410ms.
[00:02:00] Sofia Alvarez: When you say quantization profile, can you confirm this runs without changing customer data flow or storage? We need to verify encryption-at-rest and KMS usage.
[00:02:09] Priya Desai: Yes, quantization only affects model weights in memory on the serving nodes. Data in transit and at rest still follows the same encryption policies; we don't persist your inputs. We'll send a short note on the KMS flow and where keys live.
[00:02:22] Ethan Brooks: Can we get the exact delta in predicted scoring? Claire, we care about customer-visible quality.
[00:02:27] Claire Huang: Yeah a 1-2% BLEU-ish or whatever is fine for chat but we need to see regression tests against our top-200 prompt set.
[00:02:35] Priya Desai: We ran your top-200 offline; the quantized model had an average 0.8% drop on the score you provided. I'll attach the CSV to the runbook.
[00:02:42] Alex Morgan: Good. Back to the spike: Priya, you traced the GC event—was that host-level or runtime?
[00:02:49] Priya Desai: Looks like a host-level kernel swap while the node hit a temporary memory pressure due to an unrelated container's OOM event. We've suggested a node taint / pod isolation policy and stricter resource limits for co-located services. Marcus, can you comment on how feasible that is before we cutover?
[00:03:06] Marcus Lee: It's doable; we can cordon the GPU pool for the pilot nodes during the safety window. We need 48 hours notice for maintenance windows, but for the 2% canary we can do a short quiet window.
[00:03:18] Claire Huang: What about autoscaling? We saw some delayed ramps causing queueing.
[00:03:22] Priya Desai: We recommend a faster scale trigger for the serving group: reduce the CPU/queue thresholds and enable warm standby instances rather than cold spin up. That reduces warmup latency but costs more; we can configure burst capacity policy to match your budget cap.
[00:03:36] Ethan Brooks: Let's talk canary percentages. We proposed A/B at 2% traffic shift to Redwood variant and 98% to current. What's the rollback criteria?
[00:03:45] Alex Morgan: Rollback triggers we suggest: p95 increases >25% from baseline, error rate >0.5% elevated for 3 consecutive minutes, or user-facing regression in top-200 prompt set failure rate >2%. Also an ops/manual stop if any security alert is raised.
[00:04:00] Sofia Alvarez: For security alerts: we need a stream of audit logs and an SLA on log delivery. How long are logs retained?
[00:04:06] Priya Desai: By default Redwood retains request metadata and trace for 30 days in the hosted plan; for dedicated/private you can configure retention. We'll send a table of retention options and S3 export hooks with encryption.
[00:04:19] Claire Huang: Ok fair. Priya, can you quickly walk through the proposed runbook steps for a canary cutover?
[00:04:24] Priya Desai: Sure. High level: 1) Pre-cutover: confirm canary image and config pinned, shadow run for two hours with X% traffic mirror, validate telemetry and alerting. 2) Canary: shift 2% traffic using A/B routing with header split, observe metrics for 60 minutes. 3) Ramp: if checks pass, progressively 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 30 minute holds. 4) Rollback: immediate route back to baseline if triggers hit, and run postmortem. We'll include exact playbook steps, console links, and a checklist in the runbook doc.
[00:05:02] Marcus Lee: For the traffic mirror you mentioned, can that capture request bodies for our quality checks? We have concerns about PII.
[00:05:10] Priya Desai: Mirror can redact or hash specified fields. For PII we recommend field-level redaction and we can hash identifiers so you can match traces without storing raw PII in Redwood logs.
[00:05:22] Sofia Alvarez: That sounds good, but we need to ensure the hash is deterministic and reversible only on your side? Or reversible on our side?
[00:05:28] Priya Desai: Hashing is deterministic; if you want two-way encryption we suggest tokenization where keys live in your KMS—Redwood will store the tokenized value only. We'll include the options in the security note.
[00:05:40] Alex Morgan: On monitoring—Priya, which dashboards should we watch during the first 2% canary?
[00:05:45] Priya Desai: The essentials: request rate, median/p95/p99, error rate, model tokenization errors, cache hit ratio, and the canary-specific delta panels comparing baseline and canary. We will provide a pre-packaged Grafana dashboard link.
[00:05:58] Ethan Brooks: Also surface UX metrics: latency tail mapped to user retry rate because we've seen web client do retries after 400ms.
[00:06:05] Priya Desai: Yep, we'll add retry breakdown and synthetic user journeys in the dashboard.
[00:06:10] Claire Huang: Are there costs we should expect when running the burst policy / warm standby? Need to budget.
[00:06:15] Alex Morgan: We'll provide an estimated burn rate for standby instances and quantization tradeoffs. It will be a small percent bump for the pilot; we'll include a per-hour estimate in the runbook.
[00:06:24] Marcus Lee: Looking at the benchmarks you sent, one window had a weird spike at 2:14am; can you share the traces for that window again?
[00:06:31] Priya Desai: I'll attach the full trace bundle to the ticket. There was a kernel recompile plus the host OOM event mentioned earlier. Some of the transcription in the logs shows 'KV cash' which confused the team, lol.
[00:06:42] Claire Huang: (laughs) okay.
[00:06:45] Alex Morgan: Let's cover test plan: Marcus, you'll run a 6-hour production-pattern test between 9pm-3am to reproduce the burst. Priya will monitor and we will collect traces. If p99 > 300ms we'll stop and iterate on batching.
[00:07:01] Marcus Lee: Confirmed, I'll schedule and attach traces.
[00:07:04] Sofia Alvarez: On compliance: can you provide the certificate and the audit contact? We need a contact for the SOC2 report exchange.
[00:07:10] Alex Morgan: Yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and a contact at Redwood security. Expect the bundle by tomorrow.
[00:07:16] Ethan Brooks: For the canary schedule, what's the earliest we can cut?
[00:07:20] Priya Desai: With the runbook and the 6-hour bench, the earliest safe window is 2026-08-11 if we get everything by the deadlines. That gives time for security review and a dry run.
[00:07:30] Claire Huang: Works for us. One more question: do we need a DB migration or schema change?
[00:07:34] Marcus Lee: No, not for this. It's purely inference serving and routing changes.
[00:07:38] Alex Morgan: Ok, next let's talk about the A/B experiment metrics. Ethan, what acceptance criteria from product side?
[00:07:43] Ethan Brooks: Primary is no user-visible regressions on the top-200 prompt set, acceptance defined as <1% increase in failure/incorrect responses and p95 not more than 20% above baseline. Secondary: error rate below 0.2% and no security-critical alerts.
[00:07:58] Priya Desai: We'll wire those as gating checks; can run automated evaluation on mirrored traffic too.
[00:08:03] Claire Huang: For mirrored traffic eval, how fast can we get results? We need near real-time scoreboard.
[00:08:08] Priya Desai: The automated eval will give rolling stats every 5 minutes; full detailed CSV within an hour.
[00:08:13] Alex Morgan: Let's note the decision points: pre-cutover greenlight, canary pass/fail after 60 minutes, ramp decisions at each hold. We'll place a manual approval step at 30% to ensure human ops sign-off.
[00:08:24] Marcus Lee: Can we add a kill-switch route in the LB so we can flip instantly without a deploy?
[00:08:28] Priya Desai: Yes, routing uses header-targeted rules or feature flag at the gateway so you can revert instantly. We'll include run commands in the runbook.
[00:08:36] Alex Morgan: Any other blockers?
[00:08:38] Sofia Alvarez: We need confirmation that redwood will not persist raw request content beyond 72 hours for this pilot--that's our policy.
[00:08:46] Priya Desai: For hosted, default is 30 days but we can set the pilot to 72 hours and provide exports. We'll document this and apply a shorter retention for your pilot project.
[00:08:55] Claire Huang: Perfect.
[00:08:57] Alex Morgan: Ok quick recap of action items: Alex to upload runbook and SOC2 contact; Priya to prepare dashboard and canary config; Marcus to run the 6-hour bench; Sofia to confirm retention/KMS Qs; Ethan to finalize acceptance criteria doc. Any additions?
[00:09:15] Ethan Brooks: No additions.
[00:09:17] Alex Morgan: Great. We'll aim to reconvene after bench is run. Priya, do you want to demo the dry-run on Thursday?
[00:09:24] Priya Desai: Yes Thursday 11am ET works. I'll set up the meeting and invite the group.
[00:09:29] Claire Huang: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:31] Alex Morgan: Thanks all. End call.
[00:09:33] SYSTEM NOTE: Recording saved to Redwood Fireflies storage.
